chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Magra'a, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Amr ibn Saeed ibn Hilal, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I hardly ever meet you except after years, so advise me with something that I can take to it.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'I advise you to fear Allah, and be truthful in narration, and have piety (war'), and strive hard (ijtihad). And know that striving does not benefit one who does not have piety with him.'

And beware of your soul craving for those who are above you, and sufficient is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family): 'Let not their wealth and their children excite you.'
And do not stretch your eyes to that with which We have provided different classes of them, (of) the splendour of this world's life.

So if you fear any of that, remember the lifestyle of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), for his food was barley, his sweetness was dates, and his fuel was palm twigs if he found them.

And when you are afflicted with a calamity, remember your affliction with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), for the creatures have never been afflicted with the like of what he (peace be upon him) was afflicted with, at all.
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical teachings for spiritual growth according to Imam al-Sadiq in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines a comprehensive spiritual framework for his companion, emphasizing that *war'* (ascetic piety) is the necessary condition for *ijtihad* (spiritual striving) to be effective. He contextualizes this by contrasting worldly abundance with the Prophet’s modest lifestyle, urging the companion to cultivate contentment by reflecting on the Prophet’s simple sustenance and to find solace in grief by comparing personal losses to the unparalleled tragedy of the Prophet’s death.
